# Wiki Sitemap Cell Grammars

The grammars an `information-architecture` page's sitemap table takes, and the rules across its rows and across the pages it includes. `wiki-cell-grammars` holds how a template declares a grammar, and the rules every grammar shares.

**See also:** `wiki-authoring-spec` — for the readability rules and the list of every author-facing lookup.
**See also:** `wiki-cell-grammars` — for the `Cells:` label, pending cells and what stays judgment.
**See also:** `wiki-surface-placement-cell-grammars` — for the surface bullets that cite a node.

## Sitemap cell grammars

The table under `## Sitemap / structure` holds one row per node, with the columns Node, Label, Parent, Reached by, Route, Lands on, Also under, Shown to, Order, Group and Icon. A cell that does not apply reads `None.`.

- **Node** — `kebab-id`: a lowercase kebab id, unique on the page.
- **Label** — the term users see. It is a Label of the page's Taxonomy & labeling table; no grammar reads it, and `sitemap-structure` checks it.
- **Parent** — `node-ref`: `None.` for a root, otherwise the node above this one.
- **Reached by** — one of `global`, `local`, `contextual` or `utility`:
  - `global` is the top tier, reached from every page;
  - `local` is the current branch's siblings and children;
  - `contextual` is links inside a page's content, never local navigation;
  - `utility` is secondary tools, reached from every page.
- **Route** — `None.`, or a path led by `/` whose dynamic segments are written `:name`, as in `/orders/:id`. A route extends its Parent's route. Where the Parent's Route is `None.`, it extends the nearest ancestor's route, and where no ancestor has one it begins at `/`.
- **Lands on** — `node-ref`: the child a node opens to, a node on this page whose Parent is this node. `None.` otherwise.
- **Also under** — `node-refs`: `None.`, or `node-ref` values separated by `;`. `None.` is never mixed with a node (`node-refs/none-mixed`). List a second parent only where a card sort, tree test or usability test shows users splitting.
- **Shown to** — `role-names`: `everyone`, or role names separated by `,`. Each is an entry of the role catalog at `product:catalogs/roles`; `everyone` is never mixed with a role.
- **Order** — `order`: a positive integer. Orders are unique among the siblings of a composed sitemap.
- **Group** — `group-id`: a kebab id or `None.`. A group gathers siblings visually and shows no heading, and the siblings of one group sit next to each other in Order. A group that shows a heading is a node whose Route is `None.`, its members its children. A node whose Route and Lands on are both `None.` is a heading the navigation shows as a group; which of its children the journey walk counts reached is `wiki-journey-cell-grammars` § Warnings read over journeys.
- **Icon** — `icon-name`: `None.`, or an entry of the catalog the design system names in `icon-catalog:`.

**`node-ref`** is `None.`, a node id on this page, or `[[design:information-architecture/<page>]] <node-id>` for a node on another page. The audit errors on a link to a page that is not an `information-architecture` page, on a node the page lacks, and on a bare id where the cell sits off an information-architecture page, as a surface's Node cell does.

**A catalog's entries** are the cells of its code column, backticks removed: `Code`, unless the catalog's `code-column:` names another, read across every table under its `## Entries`. The audit errors on a value that is no entry, on a catalog the grammar needs and the page does not name, and on a table under a read catalog's `## Entries` that lacks the code column. The engine reads no lifecycle column, so a retired entry still resolves.

**Moved routes.** When a node's route changes, the old route stays reachable: the page records the old route and where it redirects in Decisions. A redirect to an external target stays out of the table.

### How a surface cites a node

A surface's Node bullet takes `node-refs` in its page form only: `[[design:information-architecture/<page>]] <node-id>` values separated by `;`, or `None.`. A bare id is an error (`node-refs/no-page`), and so is `None.` mixed into a list (`node-refs/none-mixed`).

A composition is an `application` page's composed sitemap, on each platform that page lists. The surface lists one node per application it is placed in:

- On each screen platform the surface lists, where its Container is `page` and its kind is not `step`, the listed nodes inside one application's composed sitemap number exactly one. The platform copy applies if there is one, otherwise the shared bullet. A surface shared by two applications that place it differently lists both nodes, `[[design:information-architecture/hosting]] settings; [[design:information-architecture/local]] settings`.
- Each listed node is on an information-architecture page whose `platforms` covers that platform. Two listed nodes on one page are an error, whether or not an application includes the page.
- Where the Container is `dialog` or `panel`, the kind is `step`, or the surface lists no screen platform, the Node is `None.`. How such a surface is placed in an application is `wiki-surface-placement-cell-grammars` § Surface placement cell grammars.

Use a platform copy of Node when the node differs by platform, and a list when it differs by application. A copy cannot name an application, because a copy qualifier is a platform.

`surface-placement` errors on a missing Node where one applies, on a Node where none does, and on a count other than one. `surface-unreached` warns of a listed node that no application's composed sitemap includes on the platform, once some application page lists that platform. `sitemap-node-coverage` warns of a node no surface cites in the composed sitemaps, except a node whose Route is `None.` and a node with a Lands on; a surface that lists several nodes credits each.

### Composition by inclusion

A page's `kind` is `skeleton`, `part` or `application`. An application lists the pages it composes in `includes:`, naming only skeleton and part pages whose `platforms` cover its own. Inclusion is transitive, and a cycle is an error. A page's **composed sitemap** is its own nodes and those of every page it includes, directly or indirectly. These checks read it:

- a Parent or Also under naming a node outside the composed sitemap is an error;
- two siblings in the composed sitemap with one Order is an error;
- `opens-on:`, a `node-ref` naming the node the application opens on, is required on an application, refused on a skeleton or part, and resolves inside the composed sitemap;
- `journeys:` is allowed on an application only.

The drawing of the table is derived into `_derived/graph-sitemaps.md`; nothing on the page is drawn by hand.
